acceptance_criteria: Holm-adjusted SPX-on-DGS10 slope p-value below 0.05 (one-sided, negative direction)
Split-half replication: the first-half and second-half slopes are both negative with one-sided HC0 p-values below 0.05
spec.alternative_hypothesis: The SPX CAR on DGS10 CAR cross-event slope is negative, with R-squared at least 0.05 and a split-half replication in the second half of events.
spec.benchmark: Zero-slope null: the target leg's CAR is unrelated to the DGS10 CAR across events (intercept-only model)
cost_assumptions: No cost gate applies: an event study measures announcement responses, not a forecast, and there is no trading rule to cost. A significant CAR is evidence about how markets respond to scheduled announcements, not a tradable edge.
spec.cost_model: No cost gate: an event study measures announcement responses, not a forecast; there is no trading rule to cost
exclusions: Unscheduled meetings, cancelled meetings, conference calls and notation votes are excluded (same event set as H0007).
FOMC minutes releases are not events in this study.
Events with an incomplete estimation window ([-60,-11]) or event window ([0,+1]) are excluded and counted.
Bars outside the sample (2003-01-02 to 2020-05-15) are out of sample for the main tests; the extended-sample regressions (to 2026-11-16) are descriptive only.
fixed_parameters: event_source=federalreserve fomchistorical pages 2003-2020 and fomccalendars.htm 2021 onwards
split_half_rule=chronological median split (first half = first floor(n/2) events)
statement_time=14:00 ET on the last meeting day
known_confounders: The DGS10 CAR is only a proxy for the policy surprise, not the surprise itself: no free federal funds futures surprise series exists.
The two CARs are measured over the same event window: the regression is contemporaneous, not a lead-lag claim, and common shocks on FOMC days move both legs.
Cross-event association is not causal identification.
The cross-section is small (about 135 events); each split-half has about 67 events.
TYVIX was discontinued in May 2020; the main sample ends 2020-05-15 and excludes the post-2020 hiking cycle.
FRED publication lag is not modelled; available_at equals the close.
spec.mechanism: A hawkish policy surprise raises the discount rate and tightens financial conditions, so equities fall when rates rise on announcement days; the cross-event slope captures that transmission. The DGS10 event-window move is only a proxy for the policy surprise, not the surprise itself: there is no free federal funds futures surprise series (a Kuttner-style surprise needs futures data). This study tests the cross-sectional association between the rates leg and the other legs, not a causal surprise effect.
spec.missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count. Events whose t=0 is absent from the panel or whose estimation or event window does not fit inside the panel are excluded and counted (same event set as H0007).
model_definition: Cross-event OLS of the target leg's CAR[0,+1] on the DGS10 CAR[0,+1], heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC0) standard errors via newey_west_hac with max_lag=0
One-sided primary p-value derived from the HAC t-statistic as Phi(t) for the 'less than' direction; two-sided p-values for the VIX and BAA10Y slopes
Holm family of 3 tests (a SPX on DGS10, b VIX on DGS10, c BAA10Y on DGS10)

Split-half replication: events ordered chronologically, first half = first floor(n/2) events, second half = the rest; replication requires both halves to show a negative slope with a one-sided HC0 p-value below 0.05
Descriptive extended-sample regressions (non-TYVIX legs to 2026-11-16), not in the test family
spec.multiple_testing_family: Cross-event CAR transmission (3 tests: a SPX CAR on DGS10 CAR slope < 0, b VIX CAR on DGS10 CAR slope != 0, c BAA10Y CAR on DGS10 CAR slope != 0)
spec.null_hypothesis: The SPX CAR is unrelated to the DGS10 CAR across FOMC events: the cross-event slope is zero.
spec.primary_metric: R-squared of the SPX CAR on DGS10 CAR cross-event regression
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted SPX-on-DGS10 slope p-value at or above 0.05 (one-sided, negative direction)
Split-half replication fails (either half's slope is non-negative or its one-sided HC0 p-value is at or above 0.05)
spec.research_question: Across scheduled FOMC events, is the SPX event-window CAR negatively related to the DGS10 event-window CAR (a rates-up surprise coinciding with equities down), and do the VIX and BAA10Y CARs co-move with the DGS10 CAR?
spec.target_definition: Cross-event regression targets: SPX CAR[0,+1] (primary), VIX CAR[0,+1] and BAA10Y CAR[0,+1], each regressed on the DGS10 CAR[0,+1] across scheduled FOMC events
spec.title: Across FOMC events, rates and equity CARs move oppositely
